title: The Federal Reserve sends a troubling signal to S&P 500 investors
summary: The Fed is sending a message to stock investors, and Wall Street is starting to listen.
content: Wall Street spent most of 2025 arguing that stocks were too expensive. That argument is fading fast. The S&P 500’s forward price-to-earnings ratio started 2026 at 22 and had already dropped to 17.7 by Nov. 5, its lowest level since November 2023, according to FactSet. There’s a twist, though. Most of that drop came from rising profit forecasts, not falling prices, with forward earnings estimates up far more than the index this year. The selloff since then has pushed the multiple lower still, and the Fed is a big reason investors aren’t rushing to pay up again. Fed officials keep sounding the alarm The hawkish turn has been building for weeks. When the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% on Oct. 28, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented because they wanted a quarter-point hike instead, according to the Federal Reserve. Two dissents in favor of tighter policy signaled to markets that the debate had already shifted. Also read: The Fed sees a new threat to the U.S. financial system New York Fed President John Williams has added his voice to the hawkish chorus, warning that inflation risks are elevated and that price stability remains the Fed’s priority. Coming from one of the Fed’s most senior officials, that tone has been hard for traders to ignore. Cook has been pushing in the same direction. On Nov. 20, she warned that waiting too long to raise rates could leave the Fed behind the curve, according to the Federal Reserve. It’s the kind of message that keeps a lid on how much investors are willing to pay for future profits. Big banks have taken the hint. J.P. Morgan economists dropped their earlier view of a single hike and now expect quarter-point increases in December, January and March. If that plays out, borrowing costs will keep climbing well into 2027. Why tighter money hits valuations hard Fed Governor Christopher Waller went further than most of his colleagues. On Nov. 10, he said a half-point hike should be considered at the Dec. 8-9 meeting and warned that “hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk,” according to the Federal Reserve. Talk like that changes the math on just about every stock in the market. The logic is pretty simple. When rates rise, future earnings are worth less in today’s money, so investors pay less for them. Bonds also start to look like a real alternative. That pressure showed up on Nov. 19, when the S&P 500 fell 2% for its sixth straight losing day. The AI trade makes the index more sensitive than usual. Goldman Sachs estimates the AI boom has driven roughly half of S&P 500 earnings growth. Many of those companies are relying on debt to fund data centers, so if financing gets pricier, the hit falls on ordinary shareholders as well, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Nvidia showed how jumpy things have become. Shares lost about 14% on Nov. 20, then jumped more than 31% on Nov. 23, yet still sat well below their October record. Swings like that rarely make investors comfortable paying a premium, even for a company with Nvidia’s growth. The hawkish turn has been building for weeks. Spencer Platt / Getty Images Are stocks actually cheap now? That depends on the yardstick you use. FactSet’s Nov. 5 reading put the forward P/E below its five-year and 10-year averages but still above its 15-year, 20-year and 25-year averages. In other words, stocks look cheaper than they’ve been lately, but not cheap by long-run standards. Tech has taken the biggest reset. The information technology sector’s forward P/E fell to its lowest level since March 2020, back when the pandemic was crushing markets, FactSet reported. For a group that carried most of this bull market, that’s a sharp change in mood. More Fed: Scott Bessent just reframed the case for a December rate hike Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reveals October surprise inside interest-rate pause How a Fed interest rate pause would impact Main Street investors Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson thinks the pullback isn’t quite finished. He expects the S&P 500 to bottom in the 7,100 to 7,300 range before turning higher into year-end and 2027. He isn’t telling clients to hide, though, and suggests adding exposure to higher-quality semiconductor stocks that have sold off but still show strong earnings. What investors are watching before Dec. 9 The latest inflation data didn’t offer much relief. The PCE price index, the Fed’s preferred gauge, rose 3.8% from a year earlier in October, while core PCE came in at 3.3%. September’s headline reading was 3.6%. Economists read that as a green light for the hawks. Heather Long of Navy Federal Credit Union said inflation is back near a three-year high and that progress in cooling has stalled. Traders now see a December hike as close to certain. Next up is the November jobs report on Dec. 4, then the Fed’s decision on Dec. 9. Futures traders already price in at least two more quarter-point hikes by July 2027. Unless the data cools soon, investors may keep demanding a lower multiple before they’re willing to own stocks. title: Social Security taxes: 3 income traps costing retirees thousands
summary: Three common retirement income traps trigger the tax torpedo: here's how to avoid them.
content: Most retirees expect a federal tax break once they stop working, yet millions end up owing income taxes on up to 85% of their Social Security benefits. That surprise stems from a calculation the IRS calls provisional income , also referred to by the Social Security Administration as combined income. Because the statutory thresholds governing benefit taxation have not been adjusted for inflation since Congress established them in 1983 and 1993, routine annual cost-of-living adjustments push more retirees into taxable tiers. To determine whether your benefits are taxed, the IRS adds your adjusted gross income (excluding Social Security), any tax-exempt interest, and 50% of your annual Social Security benefits. Filing Status 0% of Benefits Taxable Up to 50% Taxable Up to 85% Taxable Single / Head of Household $25,000 or less $25,001 – $34,000 Over $34,000 Married Filing Jointly $32,000 or less $32,001 – $44,000 Over $44,000 Married Filing Separately (lived with spouse) — — Over $0 (any positive income) Keep in mind that “85% taxable” does not mean you face an 85% tax rate; rather, up to 85% of your benefits are added to your taxable income and taxed at your ordinary marginal rate. Crossing these limits triggers the “tax torpedo,” where extra outside income pulls a larger share of your Social Security check onto your tax return. It’s important for retirees to understand the Social Security tax torpedo and how it can cost you. Watch out for 3 common income traps involving Social Security and taxes 1. Taking lump-sum traditional IRA or 401(k) withdrawals Every dollar withdrawn from a pre-tax retirement account counts directly toward your provisional income. Pulling out $15,000 or $20,000 in a single year for a major expense such as a roof replacement, medical bill, or vehicle can push your income over the upper threshold and trigger a steep jump in your effective tax rate. For example, if you sit in the 12% federal bracket above the upper threshold, an extra $1,000 traditional IRA withdrawal doesn’t just generate $120 in tax. More Retirement: Annuities can be a retirement safety net to prevent outliving savings How retirees over 70½ can cut RMD taxes with a QCD Self-directed IRA pitfalls: one mistake can blow up your retirement It also exposes an additional $850 of Social Security benefits to taxation, creating an effective marginal rate of 22.2% on that withdrawal. To avoid this spike, tap Roth IRA or Roth 401(k) balances for lumpy expenses, since qualified Roth distributions are excluded from provisional income. 2. Assuming municipal bonds are completely tax-free Retirees frequently load up on municipal bonds for federally tax-exempt income, overlooking that the IRS explicitly adds tax-exempt interest back into the provisional income formula. While the bond interest itself remains free from direct federal income tax, those payouts still inflate your provisional income. For instance, $5,000 in municipal bond interest can push a married couple past the $44,000 ceiling, forcing up to $4,250 of previously untaxed Social Security benefits onto their Form 1040. Holding yield-heavy fixed income inside Roth accounts — or pairing taxable brokerage holdings with strategic tax-loss harvesting — often keeps provisional income lower than relying solely on municipal bond yields. 3. Ignoring pre-tax balances until RMD age Deferring all retirement withdrawals until Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs) begin at age 73, or age 75 for those born in 1960 or later, often creates a mandatory income surge stacked directly on top of Social Security. Those compounding withdrawals do more than lock your benefits into the 85% taxation tier. Large RMDs can also phase out the $6,000 per-person senior bonus deduction (which begins phasing out above $75,000 in modified adjusted gross income for single filers and $150,000 for joint filers) and trigger higher Medicare IRMAA premium surcharges. Instead of waiting, use lower-income “gap years” after retiring and before claiming Social Security to execute partial Roth conversions at lower tax brackets. Once you reach age 70½, you can also use Qualified Charitable Distributions (QCDs) , up to the $111,000 annual limit, to send IRA funds directly to charity. This satisfies your RMD without adding a dime to your provisional income. Protecting your retirement check A little proactive tax mapping goes a long way toward shielding your monthly check. Each fall, project your provisional income before taking year-end distributions, blend pre-tax and Roth withdrawals to stay below key thresholds, and start trimming large pre-tax balances well before mandatory RMD rules take over. title: How much GOOGL stock does Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai own?
summary: Sundar Pichai has worked at Alphabet for more than two decades and has served as CEO since 2019. Here’s how many Alphabet shares he owns.
content: Sundar Pichai is only the second CEO of Alphabet (formerly Google) since the company, which made internet search synonymous with its eponymous founding name, was created in 1998. Pichai was hired six years after Google got its start, and he has led product and engineering for Google’s products and platforms, including Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail, and Google Workspace. Since 2019, he has held CEO titles for the Google division and its holding company, Alphabet. Here’s how many Alphabet shares Pichai owns and how he accumulated them. How much of Alphabet does Sundar Pichai own? Pichai owns 3.2 million shares of Alphabet, according to an SEC filing in October 2026 . That amount consisted of direct ownership of 1,678,737 shares of Class C Capital Stock, 191,759 Class C Google stock units, and 227,560 shares of Class A common stock. Pichai’s indirect ownership included 1.1 million shares of Class C Capital Stock held in annuity trusts by him and his wife, Anjali. Class C shares, which use the ticker symbol GOOG, hold no voting shares, while Class A shares, which trade under the GOOGL symbol, have voting shares. Class B shares aren’t publicly traded but hold significant voting power, and almost all of that stock is held by founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin. Together, the two hold the majority of voting power over Alphabet. Related: How much ANT stock does Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei actually own? Is Sundar Pichai the largest individual shareholder of Alphabet? Sergey Brin and Larry Page are the largest individual shareholders of Alphabet, and their ownership is spread across the company’s three classes of stock. Brin holds 717.8 million shares in Class A, B, and C common stock through both direct and indirect ownership, based on an SEC filing in August 2026 , and that equates to almost 5.9% of the total 12.24 billion outstanding shares. Alphabet’s largest institutional shareholders Institutions own about 89.8% of Alphabet’s GOOGL stock, according to Nasdaq data . The Vanguard Group is the biggest holder, with 528.9 million shares, followed by BlackRock (459.0 million shares), and Vanguard Capital Management (384.8 million shares). Related: How much CRM stock does Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff actually own? How & when did Sundar Pichai accumulate his Alphabet stock? Pichai’s accumulation of Alphabet stock comes from his more than two decades of employment at Alphabet. Pichai, 53 years old, first joined Alphabet in 2004, when he served as head of product management and development, and rose through the ranks to become CEO of Google, the company’s services and cloud division. Then, in 2015, he became the CEO of Alphabet, Google’s holding company, succeeding Brin in 2019. How much stock does Sundar Pichai get as part of his compensation package? Not unlike many CEOs, Pichai takes a salary and gets incentives for meeting his company’s internal performance targets. In 2025, he received no bonuses or stock awards, but had a base salary of $2 million and $8.98 million in compensation, which included contributions to a 401(k) plan and personal use of company aircraft and a company car, according to Alphabet’s 2026 proxy statement . title: JPMorgan Chase launches 2-week mortgage rate sale
summary: You can receive a mortgage rate discount as high as 0.25% from Nov. 30 to Dec. 13.
content: High mortgage rates have been a major deterrent to buying a home in 2026. The 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.21% as of Nov. 25, according to Freddie Mac . Frankly, many Americans simply cannot afford monthly mortgage payments at that rate. But Chase Home Lending is offering prospective buyers and existing homeowners a limited-time opportunity to lower their mortgage rates. The mortgage and home-financing division of JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., is launching a two-week mortgage rate sale, from Monday, Nov. 30, through Sunday, Dec. 13. You could receive a rate discount as high as 0.25% on either a mortgage for a new home or a refinanced mortgage. “As millions of holiday shoppers look for the best online deals, the biggest purchase most people will ever make deserves the same kind of careful shopping,” Erik Schmitt, head of consumer direct sales at Chase Home Lending, said in a statement shared with TheStreet. How the Chase mortgage rate sale works If you get a mortgage or refinance with Chase, you could qualify for a rate discount of up to 0.25%. The actual discount varies depending on the borrower’s location and loan type, so not everyone will qualify for the full 0.25% reduction. When I asked a Chase representative how these factors affect the discount, they recommended that customers speak with a Chase Home Lending Advisor about their specific situation. Read more: JPMorganChase drops $750B to fix U.S. housing crisis The representative confirmed that the promotion applies to both purchase and refinance mortgages, including conforming, jumbo, FHA, and VA loans. The rate discount just isn’t available on Chase home equity lines of credit (HELOCs). To qualify for the mortgage rate discount, you must lock in your rate with Chase during the promotional period from Nov. 30 to Dec. 13. However, you don’t have to close on a house during this period. You can lock in your mortgage rate on the Chase MyHome dashboard , at your local bank branch, or on the phone with a Chase Home Lending Advisor. Chase Bank is offering a 2-week mortgage rate sale on new and refinanced mortgages. James Leynse / Getty Images Combine the rate sale with other Chase mortgage discounts A 0.25% mortgage rate discount can go a long way toward making homeownership more affordable. The discount works even harder when you combine it with other Chase discounts and programs. And yes, Chase has confirmed that you can use the limited-time rate sale in addition to other Chase mortgage deals. Let’s say you take out a $400,000 mortgage at the current average 30-year mortgage rate of 7.21%. If you qualify for the full 0.25% Chase rate discount, your new mortgage rate would be 6.96%. That would drop your monthly principal and interest payment from $2,743 to $2,675. That saves you $68 per month, or $816 annually. Now, maybe you combine that with the Chase Home Lending Relationship Pricing Program . Relationship pricing mortgage rate discounts come in several tiers, but for this example, let’s say you qualify for the full 1% Relationship Pricing Discount . Combine that 1% discount with the limited-time 0.25% mortgage rate sale, and your new mortgage rate would be 5.96%. Now your new monthly payment drops to $2,410, saving you $333 monthly, or $3,996 yearly. (Keep in mind that these numbers represent monthly payments toward the mortgage principal and interest and exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, and other housing costs.) More Housing Market and Mortgage Rates: Zillow predicts surprising mortgage rate, home price shifts Jeff Bezos says 2 policies drive up housing costs, and it’s ‘not hard to figure out’ Is the U.S. experiencing a housing recession? Experts weigh in Now for a different example. You might qualify for the Chase Homebuyer Grant , which provides up to $5,000 to eligible customers in certain parts of the U.S. You can put the $5,000 toward mortgage discount points, closing costs, and/or buying down your interest rate. By combining the 0.25% sale with the Homebuyer Grant, you could lock in an even better mortgage rate or combine a discounted rate with lower closing costs. With mortgage rates remaining above 7% , Chase’s limited-time promotion could give prospective homebuyers and homeowners looking to refinance an opportunity to secure a lower rate. And for borrowers who qualify for additional Chase mortgage discounts, the savings could be even greater. Just remember that you’ll need to lock in your rate between Nov. 30 and Dec. 13 to take advantage of the promotion. Related: Zillow reports stark housing market, homeownership shift

title: McDonald's makes key menu pricing changes
summary: McDonald's is facing a value problem from both ends of the restaurant business, and it's trying a new approach.
content: McDonald’s faces pricing pressure in two different directions and has responded by adding two new value offers. On the one hand, the chain has to fend off convenience-store rivals, which offer lower prices and have the advantage of customers having to stop there to fill up on gas. In addition, McDonald’s has to compete with sit-down chains like Chili’s, which offers its “3 For Me” deal with a sandwich, fries, and an appetizer for $10.99. That makes it hard for McDonald’s, which was once seen as a value offering, to thread the needle. Now, the fast-food giant has added a $2 breakfast sandwich deal, along with a deal that offers customers a free medium order of fries. McDonald’s adds app-only deals McDonald’s has been working to restore its reputation as being a value leader. CEO Chris Kempczinski noted that in the U.S., performance improved as the quarter progressed, with comparable sales turning positive in September, following a slightly negative result in July and August, during the chain’s third-quarter earnings call . He attributed that to a change in the company’s value strategy. “That improvement followed a series of interventions we initiated during the quarter, restoring some digital offers to drive frequency with our most engaged customers, shifting marketing support toward proven value platforms, and stepping up our focus on restaurant-level execution,” he said. Now, the chain has launched two app-only deals. Free medium fries with $1 minimum purchase: Make any day fry day. Download the app and get ’em with your purchase of $1+. $2 Breakfast Sandwich : Now you want to wake up early. Download the app and choose from a Sausage, Egg & Cheese McGriddle, Bacon, Egg & Cheese Biscuit, Egg McMuffin, and more once a week only in the app — excludes delivery. Source: McDonald’s Both offers are valid one time a week through the end of the year at participating McDonald’s. The prices exclude tax and are not eligible for delivery. To get these deals, consumers must opt in to the chain’s rewards program. McDonald’s fights to take back its value crown Fast-food chains have been struggling to prove that they offer good value for a few years. More Americans have seen McDonald’s and other chains as a luxury, according to a 2024 LendingTree survey . Some of the key findings of that survey of 2,000 Americans include: Americans love fast food, but costs are forcing them to curb their cravings. Three in four Americans typically eat fast food at least once a week, but the majority (62%) say they’re eating it less due to rising prices. In fact, 65% of Americans have been shocked by the high price of a fast-food bill in the past six months. Are burgers the new Birkins? More than three-quarters (78%) of consumers view fast food as a luxury because it’s become increasingly expensive. Additionally, half of Americans say they view fast food as a luxury because they’re struggling financially. “McDonald’s… is supposed to be an inexpensive treat or a cheap fast-food fix. It is now a relatively expensive purchase, especially for a family,” GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders told USA Today . “Many don’t think it’s worth the money, so they cut back on dining there.” More Restaurants: 40-year-old fast-food franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Landry’s rescues 9 restaurants from bankruptcy as closures mount Outback Steakhouse restaurant franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino agrees that McDonald’s has lost its perception of being a cheap dining option. “McDonald’s used to be where you took the kids when you didn’t feel like cooking. When the bill starts to feel like you’ve taken the family out to dinner, you start thinking, well, where do we actually want to go? That’s a lousy question for McDonald’s to have people asking,” he told TheStreet. McDonald’s is offering $2 breakfast sandwiches. Shutterstock McDonald’s knows it has a value problem Kempczinski admitted during the Q3 call that McDonald’s has work to do on its value offering. He shared that the chain was testing “mix-and-match bundles that give customers greater choice and provide familiar ordering behaviors for prior buy one, add one offers.” That testing is ongoing at thousands of U.S. restaurants. “Our goal is to launch a new program nationally in early 2027,” he said. The CEO is encouraged by the early results. “We’ve already made significant improvements to address holistic value across our menu, which contributed to improvement in value and experience scores across our top 10 markets,” he added. Kempczinski also defended McDonald’s pricing compared to its rivals. “Today, our base menu pricing across the industry’s most popular menu items in chicken, beef, and beverages is generally below that of our nearest competitors. Our $5 and $6 meal deals remain industry standouts, and our Extra Value Meals on everyday fan favorites have become a proven platform to drive incremental sales,” he added. McDonald’s offers strong value if you pick and choose from its menu. I find it a little hard to justify the $10.89 my local McDonald’s is charging for a 10-piece Chicken McNuggets Meal or the $12.79 price of its Double Quarter Pounder Meal, but that same location has a buy-one-get offer for a 10-piece Chicken McNuggets, which costs $6.29. In theory, I could build two McNuggets meals for less than buying the combo off the menu. That’s confusing and not the best look for the chain, but it’s also a true value that consumers may embrace. title: Mall retailer with 88-year history closes huge key store, cuts jobs
summary: Shoppers have limited days left to grab 50% discounts at the Dillard's clearance hub before the entire property changes.
content: Traditional department stores have spent years fighting for survival as shopping habits shift online and away from enclosed malls. Recent federal data confirms the battle is ongoing. While total U.S. retail and food services sales climbed 5% during the first 10 months of 2026 compared to the same period a year earlier, department store sales rose just 0.7%, according to the U.S. Census Bureau . That broader shift has reshaped how rival chains manage their stores. Upscale competitor Nordstrom recently shut down its deep-discount clearance outlet in Illinois and cut 101 jobs, marking one of several closures as it refocuses on smaller, off-price Nordstrom Rack locations in open-air strip malls, as I previously reported for TheStreet. Now, another longtime mall anchor is preparing to shut down a massive 50,000-square-foot store. Yet this closure is not a sign of financial trouble, as it is happening to one of retail’s sturdiest performers, Dillard’s. Dillard’s confirms Florida clearance store permanent closure and layoffs The Little Rock, Arkansas-based retailer confirmed in its third-quarter earnings release on Nov. 12, 2026, that its Boynton Beach Mall Clearance Center in Boynton Beach, Florida, will close permanently in January 2027. The shutdown will result in 22 permanent layoffs between Jan. 8 and Jan. 15, 2027, according to a state WARN notice filed with the Florida Department of Commerce. At 50,000 square feet, the store is one of 28 clearance centers operated by Dillard’s across its 272-store network. Normally, closing a clearance hub would raise red flags, since Dillard’s uses these outlets to clear unsold seasonal merchandise and protect full-price profit margins. Yet Dillard’s latest financial results show solid sales, pointing to a completely different reason behind the shutdown. Dillard’s is closing a key 50,000-square-foot store and cutting jobs. neiu20001 / Getty Images Why Dillard’s is closing Boynton Beach Mall Clearance Center Dillard’s earnings release did not give a reason for the closure, but the timing points to the mall’s planned redevelopment rather than weak performance. In October 2026, mall owner Washington Prime Group sent lease-termination notices to the shopping center’s remaining tenants, ordering them to vacate by Jan. 15, 2027, according to The Coastal Star . That eviction deadline aligns directly with Dillard’s planned January exit and its Jan. 8 layoff timeline. Opened in October 1985, the 91-acre Boynton Beach Mall spent more than four decades as a major shopping destination in Palm Beach County. Over the past decade, however, anchor departures and e-commerce competition hollowed out the indoor property. Following a steady decline accelerated by the Covid pandemic in 2020, the mall’s owner successfully petitioned the city to rezone the property from commercial to mixed-use, making the land more appealing to residential homebuilders. Now, one of the largest U.S. homebuilders, Lennar, has the site under contract and expects to close on the purchase in early 2027, according to Discover South Florida . Though planning is still in the early stages, Lennar has said it plans a mixed-use community led by single-family attached housing, along with retail, open space, and civic uses. Only three operators on the site, JCPenney, Cinemark, and Christ Fellowship Church, own their parcels separately and may continue operating after the main mall shuts down. For leased tenants like Dillard’s, however, it was time to move on. Malls are not disappearing completely, but major change is underway Boynton Beach Mall is part of a broader structural shift reshaping U.S. retail real estate, one in which aging enclosed malls are shrinking while open-air centers are increasingly gaining popularity. Enclosed malls carry an 8.2% vacancy rate nationwide, nearly double the overall U.S. retail vacancy rate of 4.3%, according to MMCG Invest . In comparison, open-air power centers sit at just 4.7% vacancy, and strip centers hold steady at 5.2%. As I have covered extensively in recent analyses of mall staples like Tilly’s and Journeys parent Genesco , traditional mall chains have increasingly trimmed underperforming indoor locations to protect profitability. Even off-mall players such as The Cato Corporation have aggressively pruned weaker storefronts while reshaping their footprints. Malls are not disappearing completely, though. Instead, the format is splitting into two distinct tiers: Top-tier “Class A” malls are reinventing themselves by adding dining, entertainment, fitness, and medical tenants to draw social traffic. Older “Class B and C” malls built in the 1970s and 1980s are increasingly being demolished or converted into mixed-use housing and open-air retail parks. Even when retailers close stores, open-air space gets snapped up quickly. Across all U.S. retail formats, tenants absorbed 16.4 million net square feet of space through the first eight months of 2026, proving that demand for physical stores remains healthy outside struggling enclosed malls, according to MMCG Invest . Related: Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half Dillard’s history and resilience amid retail shifts Few department store operators have shown resilience amid mall decline pressures better than Dillard’s. Founded in 1938 when William T. Dillard opened his first store in Nashville, Arkansas, with an $8,000 loan from his father, the company expanded steadily across the South and Midwest by acquiring regional chains. Today, it spans 30 states with 46.1 million square feet of retail space. Shoppers remain loyal to Dillard’s mix of upscale national brands and exclusive private labels, including: Antonio Melani Gianni Bini Cremieux Roundtree & Yorke In its third-quarter earnings report , Dillard’s reported that both total retail sales and comparable store sales rose 1% year over year. Net income reached $130.9 million, or $8.38 per share, while retail gross margin held firm at 45.3% of sales. “We achieved 1% sales growth on top of last year’s 3% increase, supporting a strong 45.3% retail gross margin,” Chief Executive Officer William T. Dillard II said in the report. Just as important is Dillard’s real estate strategy. Unlike rivals that lease most of their stores, Dillard’s owns approximately 43.3 million of its 46.1 million square feet of retail space outright, or roughly 94%, according to its 2025 annual report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission . That ownership shields Dillard’s from rent hikes and landlord evictions, making its leased Boynton Beach store a rare exception. 50% discounts and what else Dillard’s customers should know For South Florida shoppers, final bargains are already on the racks. The Boynton Beach location is advertising steep closing markdowns, including an additional 50% off the lowest ticketed prices, ahead of its January shutdown, according to Dillard’s . Visitors should also check hours before driving over, as the store operates on a reduced schedule and remains closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Once the Boynton Beach store shuts down in January 2027, Palm Beach and Broward County residents will lose their closest clearance hub. Four clearance outlets will remain open elsewhere in Florida, according to Dillard’s : Jacksonville: Regency Square Mall Clearance Center (9501 Arlington Expressway) Ocoee: West Oaks Mall Clearance Center (9403 West Colonial Drive) Orlando: Fashion Square Mall Clearance Center (3403 East Colonial Drive) Port Richey: Gulf View Square Clearance Center (9409 U.S. Highway 19) Full-line Dillard’s stores in Wellington, Coral Springs, Fort Lauderdale, Pembroke Pines, and Jensen Beach will remain open, offering regular assortments without the deep clearance-center markdowns. title: Avoid these Black Friday tricks and scams
summary: Learn when to buy what, things you probably shouldn't buy, and how to avoid getting scammed.
content: Despite changing shopping patterns, Black Friday remains a massive day for retailers, though it has become just one part of an expanded season of retail deals. “Adobe expects U.S. online sales to hit $275.1 billion this holiday season (Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026), growing 6.7% year-over-year (YoY). Cyber Week (the five-day period between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday) is set to drive $47.5 billion online (up 7.4% YoY), representing 17.3% of the full holiday season spend,” according to Adobe’s 2026 forecast . A lot of those sales, however, will be online. “Cyber Monday (Nov. 30) is expected to set a new milestone for U.S. e-commerce, with consumers spending over $15 billion online in a single day ($15.1 billion, up 6.2% YoY). The second biggest day of the season will be Black Friday ($12.9 billion, up 9.2% YoY), which is growing faster than Cyber Monday — driven in part by having the biggest discounts for categories such as TVs, apparel, and appliances,” according to Adobe’s analysis. It’s a long holiday season, and there are better days than others to buy certain items. Shutterstock When to buy what during Thanksgiving shopping season Black Friday is Nov. 27 and Cyber Monday is Nov. 30. Adobe’s data showed that there are better days than others to buy certain items. Black Friday: Best for TVs, toys, apparel, appliances, and furniture. Cyber Monday : Best for electronics and computers. Thanksgiving Day: Best for sporting goods. Peak discounts : About 30% on electronics, 29% on toys, and 23% on TVs, computers, and apparel. Some shoppers are also buying things they need rather than just things they want. “While consumers have historically embraced holiday deals to buy gifts or adopt the latest gadgets, many are taking advantage of discounts to stock up on essentials. During Cyber Week, online sales of personal hygiene products are expected to jump 150% (compared to average sales levels in September 2026) and clothing basics by 210%. Other essentials set to see a boost include baby products (up 113%), pet products (up 93%), and household cleaning items (up 49%),” Adobe reported. Also Read: Struggling home goods chain closing more stores Shopping at major retailers is a way to avoid being scammed. Shutterstock Are there any products to avoid during the Black Friday season? As a former retailer who ran a large independent toy store, I’d suggest either buying traditional stocking stuffers well before the season, or filling stockings with practical items. Something like Play-Doh or a mini Magic 8-Ball generally costs more at my former store during the holiday season. The same might also be true for staples like decks of cards, Hot Wheels, and small games. There are also some categories to avoid this time of year, according to NBC Select : Winter clothes and shoes : Wait until end-of-season clearance sales in January and February Mattresses, furniture, and major home and kitchen appliances : Wait until three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day Bed and bath linens, like sheets and towels : Wait until “white sales” in January and three-day holiday weekend sales like Presidents’ Day Fitness equipment : Wait until New Year’s sales in January. Holiday decor : Wait until after the holiday season to refresh your collection and save it for next year. ALSO READ: Walmart has a new plan to solve one of its customers’ biggest problems Holiday gift scams to watch for Back when I ran the toy store, a few days after Christmas, we would have customers bringing in train sets for us to repair. They were a brand we sold, but a lower-quality version sold in mall kiosks, or sometimes even in pop-up tents in parking lots. The manufacturer essentially put its name on a low-quality product that its actual dealers could not repair. That left a lot of people angry at us, but when our entry-level train set started around $299, and you bought one for $100, you probably should have known there was a catch. RILA Communities Foundation shared with TheStreet some other common scams to watch out for: Gift Card Scams: Scammers love gift cards because once you share the card number and PIN, your money can be gone in seconds. Never let anyone pressure you into buying a gift card or sharing the information on the back of the card. Counterfeits: Counterfeiters know holiday shoppers are looking for a great deal, and they use steep discounts, convincing photos, and look-alike websites to lure consumers into buying fake and sometimes dangerous products. Before you buy, take a closer look at who is actually selling the item, check the seller’s history and reviews, and be suspicious of prices that are dramatically lower than you would expect. Watch for misspelled brand names, poor-quality images, unusual packaging, vague product descriptions, and websites or sellers you don’t recognize. Stolen products: Beware of online sellers with little or no verifiable history and prices that are substantially lower than those offered by established retailers can indicate stolen products being resold. This is a known tactic for organized retail crime rings. A low price may be legitimate, but consumers should independently verify the seller before making a purchase. Be especially cautious when a seller pressures you to pay through a wire transfer, cryptocurrency, gift card, or other payment method that may offer limited protection. Scammers also set up fake gift-card balance-checking websites to capture card numbers and PINs. Check a balance through the website or phone number printed on the card, not through a link in a search result, ad, text, or email. “More than one-third of consumers say they have experienced at least one holiday scam tactic in recent years,” according to data shared with TheStreet by Bank of America. Scammers are also using artificial intelligence to make fake retailer and delivery-service websites look convincing. Check the seller’s history and contact details, avoid links in unsolicited messages, and contact your bank immediately if you believe your financial information has been compromised. Related: Avoid these Black Friday tricks and scams

title: It's not just REI, more retailers skip Black Friday
summary: Only a few chains close, but others opt out of offering discounts.
content: Closing on Black Friday seems like an insane move for a retailer. It’s a day when consumers are accustomed to spending, and not being open forfeits some of a retailer’s holiday sales to its rivals. REI, however, has made closing on Black Friday a marketing gimmick under the guise of doing something nice for its employees. The chain has made not being open on the big sales day part of its identity and has gotten a massive amount of publicity because of it. “When we first decided to close our doors on Black Friday, it was a leap. It meant missing one of the biggest sales days of the year so our employees could be outdoors with their families and friends. But that was the point. Choosing time outside was an act of care that reflected our values and who we are as a co-op,” REI Chief Impact Officer Susan Viscon said in a press release last year, celebrating the 10-year anniversary of the decision. REI, however, is sort of an outlier in making this decision. In fact, TheStreet could only find one other chain that shuts down on Black Friday. What we did find, however, is a number of retailers who opt out of offering special sales. These 2 retailers close on Black Friday Back when I ran an independent toy store in Connecticut, we extended our hours during the holiday season. Black Friday was just a busy day, not one of our busiest, because customers shopped the big-box stores that day. But losing any day during the holiday season was a disaster. If we had to close for a day between Black Friday and New Year’s Day, about half the sales we lost that day simply never came back. Maybe people made purchases online, or perhaps they simply didn’t buy whatever they might have purchased that day. That’s partly why, even with the good publicity REI has received for giving employees the day off, only one other large retailer has followed suit. REI Co-op Closed: On Nov. 27, all REI stores, distribution centers, call centers, and headquarters will be closed. Employees: 12,000 employees get a paid day off. Reason: REI’s 2026 release doesn’t give a business reason. It calls Opt Outside “a celebration of the many ways time outdoors brings people together.” Original reason: When REI made the closure permanent, it said “the co-op will forgo profits and sales at all locations, and instead pay its more than 16,000 employees to enjoy time outside.” Online: Customers can still browse and order online, and processing and fulfillment resume the next day. Source: REI The Ordinary (Deciem) Closed: Stores and website, worldwide. The websites of all Deciem brands (The Ordinary, Niod, Loopha, and The Chemistry Brand) and its stand-alone stores are closed on Nov. 27. Reason : In the company’s words: “We believe shopping should be slow and intentional. So should your skincare.” This year: The New York and Toronto stores become blood drive sites, and London and Copenhagen offer blood type tests. The tagline is “Not Everything We Need is For Sale.” Sources: Fast Company , The Ordinary REI has been closing on Black Friday for 11 years. Shutterstock These retailers skip Black Friday sales My former toy store did not have Black Friday sales, as most of what we sold was unique and couldn’t easily be purchased at Target, Amazon, or Walmart. We sometimes had popular items at better prices because we bought a few bestsellers in bulk, but most of our sales were made at full price. Two other major U.S. retailers have opted to open on Black Friday, but not offer any special deals or pricing. Those retailers are: Patagonia Status: Open, no Black Friday sale Reason, in its words: “Black Friday never sits well with us. Scoring a deal is great, but participating in a shopping frenzy, that’s just not our thing. We support a culture where people make careful, informed purchases.” Source: Patagonia Lush Status: Open, no Black Friday sale Reason, in its words: “Does Lush do Black Friday sales?…We’re glad you asked! The short answer is: no.” Also: The page ends with “when it comes to Black Friday, our soul is not on sale.” Source: Lush It’s about brand building Retail consultant Lisa Hutcheson told NBC New York that companies including REI, Patagonia, and The Ordinary are choosing to reinforce their brand values rather than compete on discounts. “It really solidifies with your customer who you are as a company and what your values are,” she said. “They really are trying to build their customer loyalty through their brand promise, versus just attracting bargain hunters that are out there for the day.” REI thinks that closing helps with employee morale. “I remember announcing Opt Outside at a store manager conference and seeing tears in people’s eyes,” Viscon said. “When we reopened, everyone came back refreshed, proud, and more connected to what REI stands for. We did what felt right for the co-op, and it changed everything.” Related: Avoid these Black Friday tricks and scams

title: Multi-state movie theater chain files Chapter 11 bankruptcy
summary: Scene One Entertainment also operates a 75-year-old amusement park.
content: Movie theater chains have struggled in their battle against streaming services such as Netflix, which launched in 2007, as domestic box office revenue plummeted from a peak of $11.4 billion in 2019 to about $8.8 billion in 2025, according to data from commercial real estate feasibility consultant MMCG Invest . Another major factor that led to the downturn in movie theater revenue was the Covid-19 pandemic, which shut down indoor theaters in 2020. Theaters have not recovered from that downfall. Movie theater chains continue to face declining revenue that has forced certain companies to file for bankruptcy protection. Antonio_Diaz / Getty Images Scene One Entertainment files Chapter 11 And now, movie theater chain and iconic amusement park owner Scene One Entertainment Parks LLC has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, as the owner had difficulty securing financing for its businesses. The Schenectady, N.Y.-based owner of a chain of eight movie theaters in New York, Colorado, Connecticut, and New Hampshire, and Huck Finn’s Playland in Albany, N.Y., filed its petition, along with nine affiliates, in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of New York on Nov. 22, seeking to restructure their debts. “As part of our ‘North Star ‘ to provide the best moviegoing experience in each market we serve, we have taken a critical step by filing for bankruptcy protection to secure our company’s future and ensure a path to true profitability,” Scene One Entertainment said in a statement, according to WETM-TV . Scene One Entertainment listed up to $50,000 in assets and $1 million to $10 million in debts in its Subchapter V petition. Company faced financing difficulties “A reality of our business, much like many others, is that access to capital is limited due to market conditions,” Scene One said in the statement. “Unfortunately, this has been determined to be the best path forward to restructure our debts and for our company to continue to grow, thrive, and provide the very best of Hollywood features, independent films, and family entertainment for years to come. Bottom line: we’re not going anywhere,” the statement said. Scene One Entertainment said it has no plans to close any of its businesses. All locations remain open “It is our intention that each of our locations will remain open during this financial restructuring, especially with a dynamic slate of features coming out this season starting this week,” the statement said. Scene One Entertainment was founded in 2023 by its owner and CEO Joseph Masher, who added Huck Finn’s Playland amusement park to his portfolio of movie theaters that same year, according to the company’s website. Debtor owns 8 movie theaters Scene One Entertainment operates eight movie theaters, including Market Arcade 8 in Buffalo, N.Y.; Spectrum 8 in Albany, N.Y.; Wilton Mall Cinemas in Saratoga Springs, N.Y.; Movieland 6 in Schenectady, N.Y., Greenville Drive-In in Greenville, N.Y., New Canaan Playhouse in New Canaan, Conn., Gilford Cinema 8 in Gilford, N.H., and Isis Colorado in Aspen, Colo. Masher planned to add 100 movie screens to his company’s portfolio in 2026, according to the company website, but financial issues led to the bankruptcy filing instead. Huck Finn’s Playland opened in 1951 in Latham, N.Y., and its original owners operated the amusement park until selling to furniture store Huck Finn’s Warehouse in 2014. The home furnishings retailer operated the amusement park until Scene One Entertainment bought Huck Finn’s Playland nine years later. title: Sheetz cuts gas prices as Shell, 7-Eleven offer savings for holidays
summary: Major gas station chains are rolling out limited-time holiday deals and loyalty rewards.
content: Gasoline prices are finally falling, just as millions of Americans prepare to hit the road for Thanksgiving. The national average for regular gasoline dropped to approximately $3.61 per gallon on Nov. 19, according to AAA, down about 68 cents from a month earlier. However, drivers are still paying roughly 54 cents more per gallon than they were at the same time last year. It becomes especially important as we are into Thanksgiving week, when AAA expects 72.9 million Americans to travel by car between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. With millions of drivers looking to reduce the cost of their holiday trips, major gas-station chains are offering new promotions alongside their existing loyalty rewards. Sheetz is among the latest to announce a Thanksgiving-specific discount, while Shell, Chevron, 7-Eleven, and other retailers are offering savings ranging from a few cents to $1 per gallon. But there is a catch: Some of the largest discounts require accumulated loyalty points, multiple visits or enrollment in a paid membership. Sheetz announces new Thanksgiving gas discount Convenience-store chain Sheetz announced on Nov. 24 that it will offer customers 20 cents off per gallon on fuel purchases from Wednesday, Nov. 25, through Monday, Nov. 30. The Thanksgiving promotion, confirmed to NACS , applies to all fuel grades except high-flow diesel at more than 850 locations, though Maryland stores are excluded due to state regulations. The discount is limited to 25 gallons per transaction, but customers can use the promotion multiple times during the six-day period. More Retail: Struggling home goods chain closing more stores Verizon makes changes to be more like T-Mobile used to be Home Depot drops generous offers as customers grow harder to win To redeem the offer, customers must add it under the OFFERZ tab in the Sheetz app, scan their My Sheetz Rewardz membership at the pump and accept the discount when prompted. The company also allows customers to combine the holiday promotion with other eligible My Sheetz Rewardz offers for additional savings. For a driver purchasing 15 gallons of gasoline, the 20-cent discount translates to $3 in savings. A 25-gallon purchase would save $5 before any additional rewards are applied. Sheetz is also offering My Sheetz Rewardz members one free self-serve hot or iced coffee of any size through Nov. 29, with one redemption per member. Sheetz is not the only convenience-store chain introducing a holiday-specific fuel promotion. Tennessee-based Weigel’s is offering MyWeigel’s Rewards members 25 cents off per gallon on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26. The limited-time promotions come as other major fuel retailers compete for drivers with introductory discounts and ongoing rewards. Which gas stations are offering discounts ahead of Thanksgiving? Some retailers are offering short-term holiday promotions, while others provide incentives for new loyalty members or ongoing discounts for returning customers. Here’s how the major programs compare. Company Advertised fuel savings Key conditions Sheetz 20¢ per gallon, Nov. 25–30 My Sheetz Rewardz; up to 25 gallons per transaction; excludes Maryland Weigel’s 25¢ per gallon on Nov. 26 Thanksgiving Day only; MyWeigel’s Rewards membership Kroger Up to $1 per gallon Must accumulate 1,000 rewards points Circle K Up to $1 per gallon Requires accumulating qualifying visits Shell 10¢, 20¢ and 30¢ per gallon First three qualifying fill-ups for new members Chevron and Texaco 25¢ per gallon on up to five fill-ups New rewards members; offer expires after 90 days 7-Eleven 25¢ per gallon on three fill-ups Promotional text offer; separate welcome rewards available Walmart+ 10¢ per gallon Active paid membership at participating stations Amazon Prime / BP 10¢ per gallon Linked Prime and earnify accounts Love’s 10¢ per gallon on gasoline Rewards app; location exclusions BP / Amoco 5¢ per gallon Free earnify membership Exxon / Mobil Points equivalent to 3¢ or 6¢ per gallon Earn points toward future rewards These programs have different redemption rules, and the advertised maximum discounts may not be available at every participating location. In particular, Sheetz and Weigel’s are offering time-limited Thanksgiving promotions, while most of the other discounts are part of programs available beyond the holiday. Kroger and Circle K offer some of the largest potential savings Kroger’s rewards program lets customers earn points from eligible grocery purchases, gift cards and other qualifying transactions. Every 100 points can be redeemed for 10 cents off per gallon. Drivers with 1,000 points can receive a $1-per-gallon discount on purchases of up to 35 gallons. For a driver buying 15 gallons, that would mean $15 in savings. However, reaching that maximum requires building up points before filling up. Kroger also offers a three-cent-per-gallon discount for rewards members at participating locations, even without redeeming points. Circle K’s Inner Circle program also advertises potential savings of up to $1 per gallon, but its program works differently. Members accumulate qualifying visits, including gasoline purchases of at least five gallons or eligible in-store purchases of at least $3. Those visits can be redeemed for various rewards, including fuel discounts. The available reward depends on the number of qualifying visits a customer has earned. Unlike Sheetz’s immediate holiday promotion, these maximum savings generally require customers to have already accumulated enough rewards. Thanksgiving brings limited discounts at select gas stations and convenience stores. Hispanolistic / Getty Images Shell, Chevron and 7-Eleven reward new customers Other companies are targeting drivers with discounts that can be accessed much sooner after enrollment. Chevron and Texaco are offering new rewards members 25 cents off per gallon on up to five qualifying fill-ups. The introductory offer expires 90 days after enrollment. Shell is offering new members 10 cents off per gallon on their first fill-up, 20 cents on their second and 30 cents on their third. The introductory rewards must be redeemed within 60 days of signing up and are limited to 20 gallons per fill-up. Shell also offers additional benefits through participating loyalty partners. For example, eligible AAA members linking their accounts can receive 30 cents off per gallon on their first fill-up and five cents off afterward, while eligible new AARP-linked members may receive 50 cents off on their first fill-up. Those partner offers have separate eligibility and redemption requirements. Meanwhile, 7-Eleven is advertising 25 cents off per gallon for three fill-ups through a promotional text offer. Customers can text SAVE to 711711 to access the advertised promotion . Its 7Rewards program also advertises an introductory offer of 11 cents per gallon on the first seven qualifying fill-ups or during the first 90 days, whichever comes first. After the introductory period, members can receive at least five cents off per gallon at eligible stations. The introductory promotions are especially relevant for drivers who haven’t already enrolled in the companies’ respective loyalty programs. Walmart and Amazon members can also save on gasoline Gasoline discounts are no longer limited to companies that primarily sell fuel. Walmart+ members can save 10 cents per gallon at participating Walmart, CITGO, Exxon, Mobil and Murphy fuel stations, and receive member fuel prices at Sam’s Club. Unlike free loyalty programs, Walmart+ ordinarily requires a paid membership, although some customers qualify for discounted subscriptions. Amazon Prime members can also receive 10 cents off per gallon through BP’s Earnify program after linking their accounts. The discount combines Earnify’s regular five-cent-per-gallon benefit with an additional five-cent Prime benefit. For drivers who already pay for these subscriptions, the rewards can provide additional savings without purchasing a separate fuel membership. Love’s Travel Stops also advertises 10 cents off each gallon of gasoline and up to 25 cents off auto diesel through its rewards app, although the offer is excluded at certain locations. Exxon and Mobil, meanwhile, allow Rewards+ members to earn three points per gallon of regular gasoline or six points per gallon of premium fuel. These points can be redeemed for future savings rather than automatically applied as discounts at every fill-up. The differences between these programs can be substantial. A 25-cent-per-gallon discount saves $3.75 on a 15-gallon purchase, while a $1-per-gallon reward saves $15. However, drivers should also compare the actual posted prices at nearby stations. A larger loyalty discount doesn’t necessarily mean the final price will be lower than at a competing gas station. With Thanksgiving travel underway, the savings could be meaningful for households planning several fill-ups over the holiday weekend. title: Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half
summary: There are two Target rules customers should know before buying.
content: Target is promoting its 2026 Black Friday event as an expanded eight-day sale, but shoppers looking for major discounts on flagship electronics will notice smaller price cuts than last year. The Minneapolis-based retail giant launched its main Black Friday sale on Sunday, Nov. 22, running through Sunday, Nov. 29. That schedule adds one extra day compared with its seven-day event in 2025. Behind the broader promotion, however, Target scaled back the headline ceiling on some of its most-searched holiday tech items. Target cuts Apple Black Friday savings in half In its official holiday announcement , Target said shoppers can save “up to $100 on select Apple devices” during its Black Friday event. That is half the maximum discount Target advertised during Black Friday 2025, when Apple savings topped out at $200 off select products, according to an analysis by Digital Citizen and Target’s official 2025 holiday announcement . Target’s current sale includes markdowns on specific Apple device and accessories: Apple AirPods Pro 3: Marked down to $149.99 from $249.99 , a $100 discount. Apple Watch Series 12 (42mm GPS): Reduced to $299.99 from $399.99 , also hitting the $100 ceiling. 11-inch Apple iPad (A16, 128GB): Discounted by $70 to $379.99 . Source: Target’s Weekly Ad (with price reported on the morning of November 26) At the same time, a major gaming discount vanished from Target’s Black Friday lineup. Last year, the retailer advertised a flat $100 off PlayStation 5 consoles. Target cut its Apple Black Friday discount in half. Bloomberg / Getty Images In 2026, Target’s Black Friday announcement omitted PlayStation consoles entirely, highlighting gaming deals on Nintendo, Nex, and Meta Quest instead. While Target discounted DualSense PS5 controllers by $20 to $64.99, console buyers will not find last year’s $100 markdown. There is one quiet exception in Target’s live Black Friday lineup. Despite advertising a $100 ceiling in its press release, Target discounted Apple AirPods Max 2 by $120, dropping the over-ear headphones to $429.99 from $549.99, according to Target’s product listing , though Amazon and Best Buy still undercut that price by $10, per NBC News Select . Why Target is holding back on deep tech markdowns Target enters the 2026 holiday weekend in a much stronger financial position than it held a year ago. In its third-quarter earnings report released Nov. 18, Target posted a 7.1% jump in net sales and a 5.6% increase in comparable sales, according to Target’s Q3 2026 financial release . Customer traffic rose 5% year over year, reversing a 2.2% traffic decline during the same quarter in 2025. Because shoppers are already returning to Target stores and digital channels, the chain raised its full-year sales outlook. Jefferies analysts said in a note this month that Target’s recent price cuts and focus on newness have been bringing customers back, according to Retail Dive . That momentum may leave Target with less need for aggressive loss-leader console or Apple discounts to get customers through the door. Across retail, many companies are also holding leaner inventories after tariff disruptions to protect margins, which leaves less excess stock to clear at deep discounts, University of Miami professor Claudia Townsend told NBC News Select . Instead, Target is spreading promotional dollars across mass-traffic giveaways and everyday categories. On Black Friday morning, Nov. 27, stores open at 6 a.m. local time and will hand out gift cards worth $25, $50, or $100 to the first 100 shoppers in line, including one $1,000 gift card per store, according to Target’s Black Friday press release . Meanwhile, competitors are still using higher Apple ceilings to pull tech shoppers away. Best Buy launched its Black Friday sale on Nov. 19 with up to $250 off select MacBook Air models, while Amazon also advertised discounts exceeding $100 on higher-end Apple hardware. Knowing where rivals beat Target is only half the equation; shoppers also need to watch how consumer buying habits are shifting this week and check two strict Target rules before buying. Related: Shoppers ditch Hostess snack cakes while Uncrustables sell faster than factories can make them Shoppers are using Black Friday differently in 2026 Even when retailers trim headline tech discounts, Americans are still planning to spend heavily over Thanksgiving weekend, though what they put in their carts is changing. Nearly two-thirds of U.S. consumers, or 64%, say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their holiday shopping, up from 51% five years ago, according to the National Retail Federation . Overall holiday retail sales are projected to grow 4.2% to $1.013 trillion. At the same time, budget-conscious households are using Cyber Week sales to stock up on everyday necessities alongside gifts. Online sales of personal hygiene products are projected to jump 150% during Cyber Week, compared with September levels, as shoppers hunt for deals on clothing basics, household cleaning supplies, and daily essentials, according to Adobe’s 2026 Holiday Shopping Report . That shift plays directly into Target’s core strengths in apparel, beauty, and household goods, where the retailer is still offering up to 50% off apparel and accessories, 40% off beauty and health gift sets, and 50% off decorative pillows and throws during its Nov. 26–29 weekend wave. Two Target rules shoppers should know before purchasing If you still plan to buy electronics at Target this weekend, whether for convenience or to stack an extra 5% discount with a Target Circle Card, pay close attention to two policies that can save or cost you money: Use the Holiday Price Match Guarantee: Any eligible item purchased at Target between Nov. 1 and Dec. 24 qualifies for a price adjustment if Target lowers its own price later in the season, TheStreet previously reported . Keep your receipt or Circle account record in case Cyber Monday or December flash deals drop prices further. Watch the shorter Apple return clock: Target gives most electronics and entertainment purchases a generous return window starting Dec. 26. However, Apple and Beats products, along with unlocked or prepaid phones, have only a 14-day holiday return window, meaning items bought for Christmas must be returned by Jan. 8, 2027, rather than Jan. 24 for standard electronics, as noted by Digital Citizen . Checking competitor prices on big-ticket Apple devices and noting that early January deadlines can help shoppers avoid overpaying, or getting stuck with an unreturnable gift, during the busiest shopping weekend of the year. title: Walmart bets shoppers won't notice its holiday price increases
summary: The retail giant has slashed its "rollbacks," but its CEO thinks the chain is still doing right by its customers.
content: Walmart has quietly cut back on its rollbacks, the company’s name for price cuts, as it heads into the holiday season. It’s a change the company made after greatly increasing its discounts to help struggling consumers. “In the summer… we had just over 11,000 rollbacks in Walmart U.S. when we completed the second quarter; Sam’s Club had also invested in price, particularly in fresh food and other categories,” CEO John Furner said during the chain’s third-quarter earnings call . The cuts, he noted, were successful. “The result of that, we’re really pleased with, which is food share gains that we haven’t seen in about three years. So I think we’re in good shape in terms of customer response, but we’ll always do whatever we can to continue to lower prices as we look ahead,” Furner added. Except that’s not actually what’s happened for the holiday season. Walmart has actually slashed its rollbacks from their peak of 11,000. Walmart has cut back on its price rollbacks. Shutterstock Walmart cuts back on deals GlobalData Managing Director Neil Saunders thinks that discounts are important during the holiday shopping season. “Black Friday traditionally relies on a lot of impulse buying — people sort of snapping up deals when they see them,” he told Business of Fashion . “Even though the discounts will be there, they’re starting from a higher original price point in a lot of cases.” Circana Chief Retail Advisor Marshal Cohen put it bluntly. “Black Friday represents to the consumer the time when they feel that everybody’s got their best deals out there. This year — probably even more than last year — the consumer is looking for good deals,” he told The Washington Post . Despite that, Walmart has cut back on rollbacks. “At the end of the third quarter, we noted we have about 7,700 rollbacks,” Furner added. That’s down from the summer peak, but the CEO noted that it’s still historically high. “Again, that’s Walmart U.S. just as an example, which is still higher than our historical average. Most quarters, we’ll talk about rollbacks in the 5,000 to 5,500 range,” he added. Walmart also cited its holiday meal basket as an example of its price investments. The 26-item basket costs just over $3.50 per person, and prices for items comparable to last year’s were down about 12%, CEO John Furner said on the Q3 call. TheStreet Walmart may not need discounts RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino thinks that the number of rollbacks Walmart offers does not matter. “Walmart doesn’t need a rollback sign on every other shelf to convince shoppers it’s cheap. That reputation is pretty firmly baked in,” he told TheStreet. Furner made it clear that Walmart remains focused on price despite rising expenses. “We’re going to do everything we can, like we’ve always done to try to keep prices as low as we can, as long as we can. Our merchants, they’re thinking about mix and where we can gain efficiencies. We’ve had some cost pressures throughout the year on fuel and transportation. I think some of those will remain true as long as diesel fuel remains elevated,” he added. Miserandino thinks that Walmart’s holiday strategy comes with some risks. “But it can’t live on reputation forever. Cutting a couple thousand rollbacks isn’t necessarily a mistake if its everyday prices are still beating the competition. If shoppers start noticing that the prices aren’t as good, though, those missing little yellow signs will suddenly matter a lot more,” he added. As someone who has covered retail for over 30 years, I tend to agree with Miserandino. I assume Walmart is cheaper than Target or my local Publix. The chain doesn’t need rollback signs to convince me it offers low prices. If I shopped at Walmart, which I don’t because its stores aren’t pleasant, price would be the reason. That’s something the chain needs to be protective of, but the difference between 11,000 and 5,000 rollbacks probably isn’t something most customers will notice.
